raw_response:
Useful existing designs for address arithmetic, pointer tagging, and C interoperability

These are transfer suggestions, not claims of deployment or demonstrated usefulness. Four candidates have dated evidence from before 2016-03-31; three are supported only by live material whose historical availability remains unverified.

1. C11 intptr_t and uintptr_t — https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf
The pointer-holding integer contract could guide address conversion for integer arithmetic and C functions that accept addresses through integer parameters. Caveat: these types are optional, general mappings are implementation-defined, and altered integers need not produce valid pointers. Evidence: N1570, 2011-04-12, sections 6.3.2.3 and 7.20.1.4.

2. LLVM 3.7 ptrtoint and inttoptr — https://releases.llvm.org/3.7.0/docs/LangRef.html
These explicit IR conversions could implement a language operation that exposes a pointer as an integer for bit operations and reconstructs a pointer afterward. Caveat: mismatched widths truncate or zero-extend, and the frontend must define its API and validity rules. Evidence: versioned 3.7.0 documentation, with release date 2015-09-01 verified at https://blog.llvm.org/2015/09/llvm-37-release.html.

3. C++ reinterpret_cast — https://timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/n3337/expr.reinterpret.cast
The explicit conversion syntax and sufficiently-wide-integer round-trip rule could inform a concise, visibly low-level Swift conversion API. Caveat: implementation-defined mappings and the round-trip guarantee do not validate arbitrary modified addresses. Evidence: N3337 section 5.2.10; the original draft at https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2012/n3337.pdf is dated 2012-01-16.

4. Boost.Align 1.60 — https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_60_0/doc/html/align/tutorial.html
Dedicated alignment-testing and buffer-alignment helpers could cover common alignment checks without requiring repeated address masks in user code. Caveat: adapting this C++ design covers the alignment portion, not all address operations. Evidence: versioned tutorial and the 2015-12-17 release entry at https://www.boost.org/releases/1.60.0/.

5. LLVM PointerIntPair — https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/llvm/include/llvm/ADT/PointerIntPair.h
Its masked pointer-and-integer storage could guide a reusable tagged-pointer wrapper with explicit extraction and update operations. Caveat: available alignment bits limit the tag, and pointer alignment must meet the checks. Evidence date: unknown; only the live main-branch code was verified.

6. Rust raw-pointer and usize casts — https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/reference/expressions/operator-expr.html
The raw-pointer-to-usize and integer-to-pointer cast expressions could inform a concise language-level route through ordinary integer address arithmetic. Caveat: smaller integers can truncate addresses, and reconstructed pointers remain subject to validity and aliasing rules. Evidence date: unknown; the historical 1.7.0 page could not be retrieved.

7. Go unsafe.Pointer and uintptr — https://go.dev/src/unsafe/unsafe.go
Its arithmetic, alignment masking, and syscall-argument patterns could inform rules for manipulating addresses and passing them through foreign integer parameters. Caveat: the documented garbage-collector and same-expression restrictions are language-specific and need deliberate translation. Evidence date: unknown; only the live source was verified.
